correctness.rationale: The normalized Radon projector produces the support function (8/pi) sum bc sqrt(1-u_1^2). Volume is a mixed-volume cubic in the three perpendicular disk radii. Six repeated-index coefficients equal 2*pi from first normal-width variation. The remaining coefficient is 1/8 of a triple absolute determinant integral, reduced exactly to the convergent hypergeometric H={}_3F_2(-1/4,1/4,1/2;1,1;1). Direct expansion and quotient by (8abc)^2 yield the displayed perfect-square stability identity, valid for all a,b,c>0 with equality iff all equal. Independent determinant quadrature and nine polyhedral-hull inner approximations test normalization and volume. Finite computations are explicitly not treated as proof.

value.rationale: The mean section body volume is a natural geometric invariant in a recently developed general theory. Computing it for the whole three-parameter box family introduces a genuine nontrivial three-disk mixed-volume constant and yields a completely sharp, dimensionless, fixed-volume cubic minimizer with an exact anisotropy penalty. This is stronger and more informative than an isolated numerical box constant, providing structural stability and exact equality classification.
